# A7 — How much of the market is duplicated?

*Draft, 2026-10-18. Generated by `python -m analysis.a7_duplication`; numbers in
`report/a7_results.json`, every duplicate pair in `report/a7_duplicate_pairs.csv`.*

## Answer

**About one posting in eight is a near-copy of another; among technical IC postings it's one in
five.** 586 postings represent 512 distinct roles (13% duplication); the 270 in-scope postings
represent 219 (19%). Duplication is concentrated at Okta (23%) and MongoDB (15%). The most common
kind isn't multi-city copying but **one job description posted at several levels**. Okta's
Principal, Staff and Senior SWE postings often share a description almost word for word. The
consequence that matters most: **13 of A2's 250 closures were reposts**, the same role relisted
under a new ID within two weeks. Censoring them moves A2's median from 43 to 47 days and **weakens
the entry/mid finding to borderline** (see below).

## Method

- **Text:** descriptions with company boilerplate removed (the same corpus-learned removal as the
  skills extractor). Otherwise every Okta posting would look like every other Okta posting.
- **Similarity:** TF-IDF on 1–2 grams, cosine, all pairs within each company. At this size exact
  all-pairs takes seconds, so MinHash/LSH would only add approximation error.
- **Cross-company:** the highest similarity between two employers' postings is **0.26**. There is no
  syndication, as expected, since every posting comes straight from the employer's own ATS.
- **Threshold 0.95,** at the clear spike in nearest-neighbour similarity; 0.90 reported as
  sensitivity.

![nearest-neighbour similarity](figures/a7_nn_similarity.png)

## What kinds of duplication

| Type (threshold 0.95) | Pairs | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **multi_level**: different title, same text, open together | 44 | One JD posted at several levels | Okta "Principal Software Engineer" ↔ "Staff Software Engineer" (0.97) |
| **multi_location**: same title, open together | 25 | One role, one posting per city | Okta "Enterprise Account Executive" Delhi / Mumbai / Bengaluru (1.00) |
| **repost**: same title, reappears ≤ 14 days after vanishing | 13 | The listing closed, the role didn't | MongoDB "Software Engineer 3", gap 1 day |
| **sequential_other** | 12 | Same text later reissued under a new title or after a long gap | Okta "Senior Software Engineer – (Java & DSA)" → "Senior Java Engineer (Design & DSA)", gap 25 days |
| *same-key relisting* | 47 postings | Vanished and came back under the *same* ID | (handled in A2: the spell continues) |

At threshold 0.90: 502 distinct roles (14%), 213 in scope (21%), with the same mix of types.

| Employer | Postings | Distinct roles | Duplication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Okta | 190 | 147 | 23% |
| MongoDB | 119 | 101 | 15% |
| Twilio | 37 | 33 | 11% |
| Datadog | 14 | 13 | 7% |
| GitLab | 65 | 61 | 6% |
| Stripe | 67 | 64 | 4% |
| Elastic | 32 | 31 | 3% |
| Airbnb, OpenAI, Cursor, Postman, Cloudflare, Deepgram | 62 | 62 | 0% |

## Consequences for the other analyses

**A1 (clustering).** A1 merged postings with identical (company, skill set) and was left with 213
in-scope postings; A7 finds 213–219 distinct in-scope roles depending on threshold. The merge was
about right, so A1's results stand.

**A2 (survival).** A closure followed within two weeks by an identical new posting is not a filled
role. Refitting A2's main within-company model with those 13 closures censored:

| | Events | KM median (95% CI) | Entry/mid HR | Onsite HR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A2 as reported | 250 | 43 d (33–50) | 1.79 (1.02–3.13) | 1.98 (1.15–3.41) |
| Reposts censored | 237 | 47 d (38–50) | **1.77 (0.99–3.19)** | 1.96 (1.12–3.46) |

The onsite effect is unchanged. The entry/mid point estimate barely moves, but its interval now
touches 1, so **it should be reported as suggestive, not established**. A2's write-up is updated
accordingly.

**Multi-level and multi-location copies** stay in A2 as separate postings, since each can be a real
requisition. But they're likely to close together, so they aren't independent. The
company-clustered standard errors in A2 partly absorb this; within-company models can't.

## Threats to validity

- **TF-IDF measures shared wording, not the same opening.** Two genuinely different roles written
  from one template look identical, and one role rewritten from scratch looks new. The 0.95
  threshold errs toward the first error.
- **Repost window of 14 days is a choice.** The `sequential_other` pairs (12) include likely
  reposts under a new title with longer gaps. Counting them would strengthen, not reverse, the A2
  adjustment.
- **The panel only sees India postings.** A role posted for India and elsewhere counts once here.

## Reproduce

```bash
python -m analysis.a7_duplication
```
